key_insight: Large language models can extract useful gross brain findings from autopsy narratives to help classify neurodegenerative diseases, especially those with distinctive macroscopic patterns.
clinical_relevance: This suggests autopsy report text could support neuropathology workflows and retrospective case review, but it is not a replacement for expert diagnosis.
method: Analyzed 5,613 Mayo Clinic Brain Bank autopsies across 7 neuropathologic categories.
Used a fine-tuned LLM to convert narrative gross descriptions into 39 semi-quantitative features.
Compared CatBoost on extracted features versus a text-based fine-tuned LLM, both with age, sex, and brain weight.
evidence_signal: On a held-out test set of 562 cases, CatBoost reached 0.73 accuracy (kappa 0.65, macro-AUROC 0.92) and the text-based LLM reached 0.75 accuracy (kappa 0.68), with high sensitivity for PSP and MSA but poor performance for AD-LBD.
watch_item: Combined AD-LBD was difficult to distinguish, so performance may be weaker in mixed or overlapping disease patterns and may not generalize beyond this single brain bank.
paper_title: Diagnostic Value of Large Language Model-Extracted Gross Brain Findings in Neurodegenerative Diseases
